title: Scope each planner run to one slice with per-invocation framing

facts.note: Primary trigger: every planner decomposition invocation, known at dispatch from the role/operation. Applies to first runs with no existing plan/ and to runs whose task text has no recognizable keywords.
Supporting signal only (plan artifacts read or written); not a necessary condition — a first run may have no plan/ yet.
Supporting signal only; not a necessary condition for activation.
Needs an observer for run boundaries (session/run id) to tell this invocation apart from earlier planner runs.

values: framing inherited from a prior run
facts.note: Inherited framing, atdd-agent asks, step-1 disk persistence and coach involvement are judged from the transcript; creation of plan/_meta.yaml is diff-observable.

fires: Any planner invocation that decomposes a slice into wagons/WMBTs/acceptances.
A first planner run on a repo with no existing plan/ directory.
A planner run whose task text names the slice without words like 'slice', 'wagon' or 'decompose'.
A planner run after earlier runs have already written plan/ artifacts with different framing.
doesNotFire: Coder or tester runs implementing an already-planned slice.
Editing source code with no planner decomposition invocation.
A non-planner role reading the repo graph for context.

given: A planner invocation targets a scoped slice (plan/ may be empty or may hold artifacts from earlier runs).
when: You frame and decompose the plan for this invocation.
then: Plan only this invocation's scoped slice, with framing derived for this invocation.
prefer: Treat framing as per-invocation: different runs have different framing.
When plan/ has existing artifacts, read them via the repo graph to compose with them.
avoid: Any atdd agent ask (not in this protocol).
Any step-1 disk persistence (not in this protocol).
Creating or using plan/_meta.yaml (not in this protocol).
Any coach involvement (not in this protocol).
Widening the run beyond its scoped slice.
why: Each invocation targets a scoped slice and different runs have different framing, so framing must come from this run and the graph rather than be carried over from earlier runs.
evidence: The run's plan output covers only the invoked slice.
When plan/ existed, the transcript shows it was read via the repo graph before composing.
No framing carried over from a prior run.
No atdd agent ask, no step-1 disk persistence, no plan/_meta.yaml, and no coach involvement anywhere in the run.
verifier_detail: Term local_scope: one scoped slice per run; framing is per-invocation, read from the graph not inherited.

Term out_of_scope: excluded mechanisms: atdd-agent-ask, step-1 disk persistence, plan/_meta.yaml, coach involvement. These exclusions are unqualified (not limited to framing). plan/_meta.yaml in the diff is a mechanical finding; the others are judged from the transcript.
audit: graph: enables planner.decomposition.jtbd-vs-odi-grammar (scope the slice per invocation before framing the main job)

splitSuggestion.then: Read existing plan/ via the repo graph to compose, and do not inherit prior-run framing.
Use none of: atdd agent ask, step-1 disk persistence, plan/_meta.yaml, coach involvement.

additions.text: Widening the run beyond its scoped slice.
additions.justification: Direct corollary of 'each invocation targets a scoped slice'; stated as an anti-pattern for the planner.
Source has no activation section; derived from 'each invocation' — applies to every planner decomposition invocation, including first runs.

additions.text: Graph-based composition/non-inheritance (S006) and the excluded-mechanisms list (S007/S011) are independently testable; kept here in prefer/avoid/evidence with full force, and proposed as separate conventions in splitSuggestion.

trace.note: Also proposed as separate convention in splitSuggestion.
